title: tooling(test-source-alias): a type reference or literal text is not a clocked load
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-tesla"} -->
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6JaoGqmNfHDtRjRpMLtsG8NzYZ)_

Fixes #25766
Part of #25677 (cutover prep G, the gate half of decision F; the test-file half is #25763).

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## What this changes

One file, `scripts/check-test-source-alias.mjs`, the clocked-window rule only (`moduleLoadSites`). The ledger half of the gate (`extractRuntimeImports`, `KNOWN_UNALIASED_TEST_IMPORTS`, the vitest alias reading) is untouched.

Before this PR the rule counted every `import('x')` the import regex could see in the comment-masked text, and its only type-position guard was `typeof` in front of the keyword. Two kinds of sites were therefore read as clocked loads although they load nothing:

1. **Type references.** `type T = import('p').T` and `const s: import('p').Schema = ...` are erased by `tsc`. The new `isImportTypeReference` decides this from what FOLLOWS the call: a type reference is always qualified (a bare `import('p')` in a type position is a compile error) and its member chain is never called. A runtime `import()` is awaited, assigned, passed, or chained into a call (`.then(...)`, a generic `.then` call with a type argument, `?.then(...)`). The head cannot decide it: `{ key: import('p') }` is an object-literal load behind the same colon an annotation uses. Type arguments after the member are balanced (braces, semicolons and function-type arrows inside them included), so the token after the closing angle bracket tells a type argument list from a generic call. Only the `import(` form is read this way; `require('p').member` is the ordinary CJS spelling of a runtime load and stays a load. Anything the reader cannot parse reads as a load (the loud direction).
2. **Text.** A dynamic form written inside a string or a template body (a scanner's own test feeding it input, a child-process script) is not code. A match now counts only when its keyword is executed code: plain code in the `codeOnly` projection, or a template interpolation interior, which `codeOnly` blanks too, read from `scanSource`'s `interpolation` array. That scan runs only when a keyword is not plain code.

Both rules skip the site for the module-scope set as well, matching what the header already said for `typeof`: an erased site is neither a finding nor a compliance token. A module-top `type T = import('p').T` therefore no longer pays, on paper, for a real clocked `await import('p')` in the same file.

## Measurements

**Merged layout** (verify branch `claude/project-thread-dwhq6r-25697-verify` at 9e37acd126, this diff applied at the root with `git apply`, `node scripts/check-test-source-alias.mjs`):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| unique clocked findings (file:line) | 37 | 30 |
| the card's 7 false positives | 7 | 0 |
| new clocked findings | | 0 |
| non-clocked findings (ledger, alias) | 42 | 42, byte-identical lines |

The 7 that are gone are exactly the card's table: `spec-symbol-4650.test.ts` in plugin-calendar :58, plugin-form :50, plugin-grid :73, plugin-kanban :50, `dashboard-global-filters-spec-binding.test.ts:102`, `data-table.test.ts:66`, `ui/scripts/__tests__/check-spec-range-floors.test.ts:286`. The 30 left are #25763's real ones. No `ui/` file is edited and nothing is added to `KNOWN_UNALIASED_TEST_IMPORTS` or any allowlist.

**objectstack main** (merge base ab510f42e):

- `pnpm check:test-source-alias`: self-test OK, run OK, same green line as before (76 packages scanned, 60 registered, 55 published subpaths).
- Ledger recompute: `node scripts/check-test-source-alias.mjs --list` before and after are identical (60 of 76 packages, 295 package-dependency pairs).
- Corpus-wide reading, with no population filter: every tracked test file's sites, before vs after. main: 48 site entries reclassified, all of them removals, 0 additions. merged: 145 removals, 0 additions. Every main removal was read by hand. They are child-process scripts in template literals (`SEED_CHILD`, `WORKER_SOURCE`, `PROBE`, `DRIVER_CJS`, an `os start` stub), RuleTester-style code strings, and erased type positions (`s is import('typescript').X` predicates, `as import('node:crypto').BinaryLike` casts, `{ knex: import('knex').Knex }` annotations). None of the files is a finding before or after, because none of these specifiers is in its package's measured set.
- Gate wall time on this box: 19.5 s before, 18.2 s after.

## Self-test

New battery `a type reference or literal text is not a load (#25766)`, 21 cases. The roster floor goes from 10 to 11 batteries.

- End to end: fixture (29) `packages/clocked-type-reference` holds an alias and an annotation (type arguments carrying a semicolon) inside a test body, plus a dynamic import as template text, each putting its specifier in the measured set. A module-top alias of `@fx/core` sits beside a real `await import('@fx/core')`. Only the real load may be reported, and it must be reported.
- Shape table read straight off `moduleLoadSites`. 8 erased rows (alias, annotation, generic annotation, qualified chain with array and indexed access, parameter annotation, string, template body, `require` in a template body) and a module-top `export type` row. 9 load rows: unawaited assignment, object-literal value, awaited, `.then(...)`, generic `.then` call, `?.then(...)`, a load inside a template interpolation, a load right after an erased alias on the same line (the #12555 lesson: erasing one site must not swallow its neighbour), and `require('p').member`.

On scratch copies of the gate (repo root pinned, imports pointed at this tree; the unmutated copy shows 12 relocation-only failures, subtracted below), each mutation reds rows of the new battery:

| mutation | new-battery rows red |
|---|---|
| drop the executed-keyword test | the 3 text rows, the end-to-end text and real-load legs |
| drop the type-reference test | the 5 type rows, module-top alias, end-to-end legs, the same-line neighbour row |
| executed-keyword test without the interpolation array | the interpolation load row |
| type reference ignores a following call | the `.then(...)` and generic `.then` rows |
| a generic argument list reads as a load | the generic annotation row, module-top generic alias, end-to-end legs |
| a head-based rule (colon or equals in front means type) | the unawaited-assignment and object-literal rows |
| the type rule also applied to `require` | the `require('p').member` row |

Every erased row is reached by at least one mutation. The awaited and `?.then(...)` load rows are not reached by these seven; they stand guard against a wider erasure rule.

## Gates

Derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at 85fe6b02 (1 path, +173/-4). Exit codes were captured before any pipe. Every derived command exits 0:

`node scripts/check-ci-filter-parity.mjs`, `check-closing-keyword-parity.mjs` (+ `--self-test`), `check-comment-mask-corpus.mjs`, `check-declaration-mirrors.mjs` (+ `--self-test`), `check-position-name-fold-loaders.mjs` (+ `--self-test`), `check-scripts-symbol-anchors.mjs` (+ `--self-test`), `check-self-test-wired.mjs` (+ `--self-test`), `check-self-test-workflow-commands.mjs` (+ `--self-test`), `check-whole-set-label-write.mjs` (+ `--self-test`), `scripts/pm/bare-root-worklist.mjs --self-test`; `pnpm check:agent-test-spelling`, `check:bash32-floor`, `check:cli-command-ids`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check:driver-memory-census`, `check:entry-guard`, `check:gitlink-declared`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check:parse-guard`, `check:pm-dispatch-gates`, `check:pnpm-filter-targets`, `check:pnpm-flag-spellings`, `check:ratchet-remedy-authority`, `check:refd-timer-probe`, `check:test-source-alias`, `check:watch-hint-literal`.

Reconciled at 85fe6b02 with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --ran ran.list`: 33 derived, 33 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.

The first run of six of them exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET: `yaml`, `typescript`, `@typescript-eslint/parser` missing in a fresh worktree). After `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` all six exit 0. NOT MEASURED locally, left to CI: the two families that take a value from the workflow (`check-shard-attestation.mjs --emit`, `check-test-completeness.mjs`) and the Test Core job steps.

No changeset: the root package is private and `scripts/**` ships in no package's `files[]`. The PR carries `skip-changeset`.

## Acceptance notes

1. **Out of scope by the card, noted:** the ledger half (`extractRuntimeImports`) still reads type references and string or template text as runtime imports. That is why such specifiers keep entering a package's measured set (all 7 merged-layout sites were in it). It belongs to the vitest-alias half that the cutover adaptation commit owns. No finding is wrong because of it after this PR, since the clocked rule no longer reports those sites.
2. **Observed, not fixed (outside the card's step 1):** a STATIC import spelled as text inside a string or template at module top still counts as a module-scope compliance token. That is the fail-open direction. Measured with a scratch copy that applies the same executed-keyword test to static matches: 67 such tokens on main and 141 on the merged layout, and none of them pairs with a clocked load of the same specifier in its file. Today it hides nothing. Carrier: none.
